# graphic/CLAUDE.md — the graphics engine's rules

Applies to everything under `graphic/`, the crate that draws a graphic clip
(road map 10: `designs/adr/roadmap-10-graphics.md`; the full design is
`archive/roadmap-10.md` §5a). Build commands are the root
`CLAUDE.md`'s: `make test` and `make lint` run this crate after the core.
The crate's record is road map 10 §10.4.

## Module map

- `lib.rs` — `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`, module declarations and re-exports
  only. No implementation code.
- `diagnostic.rs` — `Level`, `Diagnostic` (`{level, message, line, column,
  frame}`, §5b) and its JSON, keys in that order.
- `images.rs` — the decoded-image cache (spec §11 G-39, #127): `Asset
  {data, digest}`, a process-wide `Mutex` map from an asset's own SHA-256
  to `Ready`/`Building`/`Refused`/`Skipped {len}`, `set_image_cache_limit`,
  `image_cache_bytes`, the doc-hidden `image_cache_builds`, `cached_kind`,
  and the builder of a stored-deflate RGBA8 PNG copy, used only when it
  decodes to exactly the original's pixmap and `imagesize` reads the same
  size. No lock is held across a decode, an encode or a usvg call; a
  build writes only while its digest is still `Building`; the default limit
  is 0, so a binary that sets none takes the original route. The doc-hidden
  `set_image_build_hook` installs an `ImageBuildHook` every build calls
  between its two locks with none held, so a test can hold a build there.
- `library.rs` — `Library`: the font set (`fontdb`, from bytes, never
  `load_system_fonts`, G-6) and the asset map (each asset keeps its own
  SHA-256; a PNG or JPEG kind is asked of the cache first), their content `version`
  (SHA-256 with length prefixes), the `measure_text` memo, and the
  crate-private `options()` builder whose resolvers record into a `Probe`
  what resvg never reports. It also keeps the face-ID → font-blob map and
  the usage set (`Usage`, `Library::usage()`, spec §11 G-46), filled by
  `select_font`, the wrapped fallback selector and `resolve_string` (image
  kinds only); each closure calls usvg FIRST and only then locks the usage
  set for its own insert, because a nested SVG asset re-enters on the same
  thread. The generic families map to bundled faces
  (`serif` Source Serif 4, `sans-serif` Source Sans 3, `monospace` IBM Plex
  Mono, G-6), and `select_font` queries only the text's own families,
  never usvg's appended serif fallback, so a missing family still draws
  nothing and is warned.
- `raster.rs` — `rasterize`, `MAX_SIDE`, the RGBA→BGRA row copy into the
  caller's strided buffer, and every warning text `rasterize` answers:
  missing family, unparseable `font-family` (the scan of attributes, `style`
  attributes and `<style>` sheets, and the family of a `font` shorthand in
  a `style` attribute or sheet), unknown href, data: URL, non-image
  asset, size mismatch. The texts are load-bearing: tests match them and
  the app shows them on the clip.
- `measure.rs` — `FontStyle`, `TextFont` (with `preserve_space`, the
  `xmlSpace` key, G-22), `TextMetrics`, `measure_text`; a generic family
  is written unquoted.
- `module.rs` — `Module` (`Send + Sync + Clone`, holds no QuickJS object):
  `compile`, the SHA-256 revision (G-13), `meta`/`schema` read through
  `JSON.stringify` in the module's key order (`{}` when not exported),
  `defaults()`, its top-level warnings (`warnings()`, G-21 (b)).
- `runtime.rs` — `Engine` (one QuickJS `Runtime` + `Context` per (thread,
  module), §5b's limits, the interrupt deadline), the `thread_local!` map
  swept by `Weak` before each call, at most `ENGINES_PER_THREAD` (16, spec
  §11 G-21) engines with the least recently used evicted after the call,
  `svg`, `Engine::parse_colours` (the stdlib's `__parseColour` per text
  under one deadline, storing nothing; G-25), `engine_count`, `HEAP_BYTES`,
  `STACK_BYTES`, `SVG_BYTES` (8 MiB, spec §11 G-20 (c)). The crate's one
  clock.
- `sandbox.rs` — the sandbox script (G-5) and the loader that resolves no
  specifier, with `IMPORT_REFUSAL`.
- `exception.rs` — QuickJS error → Diagnostic: `{name}: {message}`, the
  position from `stack` (the module's own frame first), the budget's
  sentences, what `render` returned (a string over `SVG_BYTES` refused by its
  length, before the `<svg` check). The texts are load-bearing.
- `host.rs` — the globals `__measureText`, `__assetNames`, `__warn` and
  `__namedColour` (svgtypes' named-colour table for the stdlib's colour
  parser).
- `props.rs` — `check_schema` (compile, strict; it takes a colour reader,
  which `Module::compile` builds from `Engine::parse_colours` over the
  schema's colour defaults, G-25 (a); a non-boolean `animate` on an entry
  is refused, G-41), `overlay` (render,
  lenient; every surprise a warning; an asset stored as `""` is handed to
  `render` as `null`, silently, G-42) and the schema's limits `MAX_PROPS`,
  `MAX_OPTIONS`, `MAX_STRING` and `TYPES`, which the core restates as
  `GRAPHIC_<X>` (`core/tests/graphic_ffi.rs` pins each pair;
  `tests/reference.rs` pins the numbers the reference states, and its
  typings' key cap).
- `stdlib.js`, `noise.js`, `path.js` — §5c's standard library, evaluated
  as SCRIPTS (globals) in that order before the sandbox; each under 400
  lines. `path.js` is G-31's path helpers (`getLength`,
  `getPointAtLength`, `evolvePath`): pure JavaScript, a curve measured as
  64 chords, a draw-on dashed by the longest subpath, the last paths
  memoised per engine (at most 32, at most 50,000 chords and characters) —
  a cache that changes no answer, held in a closure no module can reach.
  No helper answers `Infinity` or NaN: a path that would make one do so
  is refused in the parse sentence (five checks through one predicate,
  `finite`; `path.test.js`'s row `T8 a number that is not finite`).

## Rules

- **The crate takes bytes and answers bytes** (G-2, G-5): no file system,
  environment or network anywhere in `src/`, and no clock except the call
  deadline. `rg 'std::(fs|env|net)' graphic/src` must print nothing, and
  `rg -n 'std::time' graphic/src` must print exactly one line, the import
  in `src/runtime.rs`: the interrupt deadline stops a call that runs too
  long and feeds no pixel, so a frame stays a function of G-5's inputs.
  Tests may read files and the clock; `src/` may not.
- `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` stays in `lib.rs`.
- Every `src/` file stays under 400 lines.
- Tests are black-box in `tests/`, through `graphic::` only, and every claim
  is an oracle — a pixel read back through `common::pixel`, an exact
  message, a comparison of two answers. The one exception is
  `tests/pins.json` (road map 10 §5l), a tripwire for upgrades.
- The root `CLAUDE.md`'s FFI three-file rule does not apply here: no `rc_*`
  export lives in this crate. G1d's `core/src/ffi_graphic.rs` is its one
  caller.
- **No closure handed to usvg holds the probe lock across a usvg call.** A
  nested SVG asset is parsed by `Tree::from_data_nested` inside
  `resolve_string`, and usvg forwards our `select_font` into that parse on
  the same thread; `std::sync::Mutex` is not re-entrant, so a lock held
  across it hangs the render. Each closure calls usvg first and locks only
  for its own push afterwards. `tests/families.rs`'s nested-asset case is
  the oracle.
- `usvg::Options` is not `Clone`: build it per call with `options()`.
- **`Engine`'s fields drop in declaration order: `render`, then the
  context, then the runtime.** Reversing them aborts the process in
  QuickJS's `JS_FreeRuntime`; `tests/module.rs`'s
  `dropped_modules_engines_are_swept` is the oracle (it SIGABRTs). A
  runtime never leaves the thread that made it, and the thread map's
  `RefCell` is never borrowed while JavaScript runs.
- The module is an ES module evaluated UNWRAPPED, so stack positions are
  the file's own. The standard library and the sandbox are scripts, which
  rquickjs names `eval_script`; `position` prefers the module's frame over
  theirs (`render.rs`'s positioned-throw test and the sandbox's
  `math_random` are the oracles).
- `tests/pins.json` is re-pinned with `GRAPHIC_REPIN=1 cargo test
  --release --test pins`, only after looking at the PNGs a mismatch
  writes to `target/pins/`.
- **The modules of `tests/graphics/` are the bundled templates** (Insert ▸
  Graphic…; project.yml's "Copy Graphic Templates" lists each). Every one,
  the six fixtures included, declares `meta.category` (one of spec §11
  G-45 (c)'s four) and a one-line `meta.description` of at most 120
  characters, held by `tests/template_meta.rs`, where a new template needs a
  row in its `TABLE`. Every one
  except `common::FIXTURES` is held to spec §11 G-44 by
  `tests/templates.rs`: inside title-safe at every frame at 1920×1080,
  1080×1920 and 1080×1080, with defaults, every combination of `enum` options
  and every `string` long (`tests/templates/long_text.rs` must name each), a
  card's background static, the last frame bare, no warning, no `NaN`.

## Dependencies, and why each

- `resvg` 0.48.1, `default-features = false`, features `text`,
  `raster-images`, `svgz`: its defaults minus `system-fonts` and
  `memmap-fonts`, which reach the file system — off for G-6 (the fonts are
  the bundled faces and the package's) and G-2 (the crate reads no files),
  NEVER for size. Binary size and build time are not reasons to leave a
  feature out. `raster-images` is required: without it resvg draws no PNG,
  JPEG, GIF or WebP `<image>`.
- `tiny-skia` 0.12.0 (resvg 0.48.1's pin) is VENDORED and patched in
  `graphic/vendor/` (spec §11 PR-13): a dither stage on every gradient, so a
  gradient does not band at 8 bits. Both `graphic/Cargo.toml` AND
  `core/Cargo.toml` carry the `[patch.crates-io]` table — Cargo ignores a
  dependency's `[patch]`, and the staticlib the app links is built from
  `core/` (`a_gradient_is_dithered_through_the_ffi` guards it). The patch is
  `vendor/tiny-skia-dither.diff`, regenerated by the one command in
  `vendor/README.md` and kept byte-equal to the vendored tree; a resvg
  upgrade that moves tiny-skia re-vendors, re-applies that diff and re-pins
  `tests/pins.json`'s gradient entries.
- `serde_json` with `preserve_order`: JSON key order is part of the
  contract (the Diagnostic's and TextMetrics' keys; a module's schema).
- `sha2`: the Library's content version.
- `svgtypes` 0.16.1 (usvg 0.48.1's own pin): parse `font-family` exactly as
  usvg does, so the scan agrees with usvg on what failed; and its
  named-colour table (`__namedColour`), so a colour name means what usvg
  draws.
- `simplecss` 0.2 (usvg's own pin; usvg does not re-export it): read
  `<style>` sheets and `style` attributes as usvg does.
- `rquickjs` 0.14.0 with `loader` only: quickjs-ng 0.16.2, vendored and
  built by `rquickjs-sys`. `loader` exists for `set_loader`; the resolver
  and loader installed refuse every specifier, and none of rquickjs's own
  loaders (which reach the file system) is used.
- `png` 0.18 (tiny-skia 0.12's own decoder, already in the lock): decode as
  `Pixmap::decode_png` does and write the stored copy (G-39); still the
  pins' PNG dump.
- `zune-jpeg` 0.5 (resvg 0.48.1's own JPEG decoder): decode as resvg does,
  so a JPEG's copy is checked against resvg's own pixels.
- `imagesize` 0.15 (usvg's own size reader): check a copy's size reads the
  same as its original's.
- Dev: `flate2`, to gzip an `.svgz` asset in a test.

`CLAUDE.md`'s: `make test` and `make lint` run this crate after the core.
The crate's record is road map 10 §10.4.

## Module map

- `lib.rs` — `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`, module declarations and re-exports
  only. No implementation code.
- `diagnostic.rs` — `Level`, `Diagnostic` (`{level, message, line, column,
  frame}`, §5b) and its JSON, keys in that order.
- `images.rs` — the decoded-image cache (spec §11 G-39, #127): `Asset
  {data, digest}`, a process-wide `Mutex` map from an asset's own SHA-256
  to `Ready`/`Building`/`Refused`/`Skipped {len}`, `set_image_cache_limit`,
  `image_cache_bytes`, the doc-hidden `image_cache_builds`, `cached_kind`,
  and the builder of a stored-deflate RGBA8 PNG copy, used only when it
  decodes to exactly the original's pixmap and `imagesize` reads the same
  size. No lock is held across a decode, an encode or a usvg call; a
  build writes only while its digest is still `Building`; the default limit
  is 0, so a binary that sets none takes the original route. The doc-hidden
  `set_image_build_hook` installs an `ImageBuildHook` every build calls
  between its two locks with none held, so a test can hold a build there.
- `library.rs` — `Library`: the font set (`fontdb`, from bytes, never
  `load_system_fonts`, G-6) and the asset map (each asset keeps its own
  SHA-256; a PNG or JPEG kind is asked of the cache first), their content `version`
  (SHA-256 with length prefixes), the `measure_text` memo, and the
  crate-private `options()` builder whose resolvers record into a `Probe`
  what resvg never reports. It also keeps the face-ID → font-blob map and
  the usage set (`Usage`, `Library::usage()`, spec §11 G-46), filled by
  `select_font`, the wrapped fallback selector and `resolve_string` (image
  kinds only); each closure calls usvg FIRST and only then locks the usage
  set for its own insert, because a nested SVG asset re-enters on the same
  thread. The generic families map to bundled faces
  (`serif` Source Serif 4, `sans-serif` Source Sans 3, `monospace` IBM Plex
  Mono, G-6), and `select_font` queries only the text's own families,
  never usvg's appended serif fallback, so a missing family still draws
  nothing and is warned.
- `raster.rs` — `rasterize`, `MAX_SIDE`, the RGBA→BGRA row copy into the
  caller's strided buffer, and every warning text `rasterize` answers:
  missing family, unparseable `font-family` (the scan of attributes, `style`
  attributes and `<style>` sheets, and the family of a `font` shorthand in
  a `style` attribute or sheet), unknown href, data: URL, non-image
  asset, size mismatch. The texts are load-bearing: tests match them and
  the app shows them on the clip.
- `measure.rs` — `FontStyle`, `TextFont` (with `preserve_space`, the
  `xmlSpace` key, G-22), `TextMetrics`, `measure_text`; a generic family
  is written unquoted.
- `module.rs` — `Module` (`Send + Sync + Clone`, holds no QuickJS object):
  `compile`, the SHA-256 revision (G-13), `meta`/`schema` read through
  `JSON.stringify` in the module's key order (`{}` when not exported),
  `defaults()`, its top-level warnings (`warnings()`, G-21 (b)).
- `runtime.rs` — `Engine` (one QuickJS `Runtime` + `Context` per (thread,
  module), §5b's limits, the interrupt deadline), the `thread_local!` map
  swept by `Weak` before each call, at most `ENGINES_PER_THREAD` (16, spec
  §11 G-21) engines with the least recently used evicted after the call,
  `svg`, `Engine::parse_colours` (the stdlib's `__parseColour` per text
  under one deadline, storing nothing; G-25), `engine_count`, `HEAP_BYTES`,
  `STACK_BYTES`, `SVG_BYTES` (8 MiB, spec §11 G-20 (c)). The crate's one
  clock.
- `sandbox.rs` — the sandbox script (G-5) and the loader that resolves no
  specifier, with `IMPORT_REFUSAL`.
- `exception.rs` — QuickJS error → Diagnostic: `{name}: {message}`, the
  position from `stack` (the module's own frame first), the budget's
  sentences, what `render` returned (a string over `SVG_BYTES` refused by its
  length, before the `<svg` check). The texts are load-bearing.
- `host.rs` — the globals `__measureText`, `__assetNames`, `__warn` and
  `__namedColour` (svgtypes' named-colour table for the stdlib's colour
  parser).
- `props.rs` — `check_schema` (compile, strict; it takes a colour reader,
  which `Module::compile` builds from `Engine::parse_colours` over the
  schema's colour defaults, G-25 (a); a non-boolean `animate` on an entry
  is refused, G-41), `overlay` (render,
  lenient; every surprise a warning; an asset stored as `""` is handed to
  `render` as `null`, silently, G-42) and the schema's limits `MAX_PROPS`,
  `MAX_OPTIONS`, `MAX_STRING` and `TYPES`, which the core restates as
  `GRAPHIC_<X>` (`core/tests/graphic_ffi.rs` pins each pair;
  `tests/reference.rs` pins the numbers the reference states, and its
  typings' key cap).
- `stdlib.js`, `noise.js`, `path.js` — §5c's standard library, evaluated
  as SCRIPTS (globals) in that order before the sandbox; each under 400
  lines. `path.js` is G-31's path helpers (`getLength`,
  `getPointAtLength`, `evolvePath`): pure JavaScript, a curve measured as
  64 chords, a draw-on dashed by the longest subpath, the last paths
  memoised per engine (at most 32, at most 50,000 chords and characters) —
  a cache that changes no answer, held in a closure no module can reach.
  No helper answers `Infinity` or NaN: a path that would make one do so
  is refused in the parse sentence (five checks through one predicate,
  `finite`; `path.test.js`'s row `T8 a number that is not finite`).

## Rules

- **The crate takes bytes and answers bytes** (G-2, G-5): no file system,
  environment or network anywhere in `src/`, and no clock except the call
  deadline. `rg 'std::(fs|env|net)' graphic/src` must print nothing, and
  `rg -n 'std::time' graphic/src` must print exactly one line, the import
  in `src/runtime.rs`: the interrupt deadline stops a call that runs too
  long and feeds no pixel, so a frame stays a function of G-5's inputs.
  Tests may read files and the clock; `src/` may not.
- `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` stays in `lib.rs`.
- Every `src/` file stays under 400 lines.
- Tests are black-box in `tests/`, through `graphic::` only, and every claim
  is an oracle — a pixel read back through `common::pixel`, an exact
  message, a comparison of two answers. The one exception is
  `tests/pins.json` (road map 10 §5l), a tripwire for upgrades.
- The root `CLAUDE.md`'s FFI three-file rule does not apply here: no `rc_*`
  export lives in this crate. G1d's `core/src/ffi_graphic.rs` is its one
  caller.
- **No closure handed to usvg holds the probe lock across a usvg call.** A
  nested SVG asset is parsed by `Tree::from_data_nested` inside
  `resolve_string`, and usvg forwards our `select_font` into that parse on
  the same thread; `std::sync::Mutex` is not re-entrant, so a lock held
  across it hangs the render. Each closure calls usvg first and locks only
  for its own push afterwards. `tests/families.rs`'s nested-asset case is
  the oracle.
- `usvg::Options` is not `Clone`: build it per call with `options()`.
- **`Engine`'s fields drop in declaration order: `render`, then the
  context, then the runtime.** Reversing them aborts the process in
  QuickJS's `JS_FreeRuntime`; `tests/module.rs`'s
  `dropped_modules_engines_are_swept` is the oracle (it SIGABRTs). A
  runtime never leaves the thread that made it, and the thread map's
  `RefCell` is never borrowed while JavaScript runs.
- The module is an ES module evaluated UNWRAPPED, so stack positions are
  the file's own. The standard library and the sandbox are scripts, which
  rquickjs names `eval_script`; `position` prefers the module's frame over
  theirs (`render.rs`'s positioned-throw test and the sandbox's
  `math_random` are the oracles).
- `tests/pins.json` is re-pinned with `GRAPHIC_REPIN=1 cargo test
  --release --test pins`, only after looking at the PNGs a mismatch
  writes to `target/pins/`.
- **The modules of `tests/graphics/` are the bundled templates** (Insert ▸
  Graphic…; project.yml's "Copy Graphic Templates" lists each). Every one,
  the six fixtures included, declares `meta.category` (one of spec §11
  G-45 (c)'s four) and a one-line `meta.description` of at most 120
  characters, held by `tests/template_meta.rs`, where a new template needs a
  row in its `TABLE`. Every one
  except `common::FIXTURES` is held to spec §11 G-44 by
  `tests/templates.rs`: inside title-safe at every frame at 1920×1080,
  1080×1920 and 1080×1080, with defaults, every combination of `enum` options
  and every `string` long (`tests/templates/long_text.rs` must name each), a
  card's background static, the last frame bare, no warning, no `NaN`.

## Dependencies, and why each

- `resvg` 0.48.1, `default-features = false`, features `text`,
  `raster-images`, `svgz`: its defaults minus `system-fonts` and
  `memmap-fonts`, which reach the file system — off for G-6 (the fonts are
  the bundled faces and the package's) and G-2 (the crate reads no files),
  NEVER for size. Binary size and build time are not reasons to leave a
  feature out. `raster-images` is required: without it resvg draws no PNG,
  JPEG, GIF or WebP `<image>`.
- `tiny-skia` 0.12.0 (resvg 0.48.1's pin) is VENDORED and patched in
  `graphic/vendor/` (spec §11 PR-13): a dither stage on every gradient, so a
  gradient does not band at 8 bits. Both `graphic/Cargo.toml` AND
  `core/Cargo.toml` carry the `[patch.crates-io]` table — Cargo ignores a
  dependency's `[patch]`, and the staticlib the app links is built from
  `core/` (`a_gradient_is_dithered_through_the_ffi` guards it). The patch is
  `vendor/tiny-skia-dither.diff`, regenerated by the one command in
  `vendor/README.md` and kept byte-equal to the vendored tree; a resvg
  upgrade that moves tiny-skia re-vendors, re-applies that diff and re-pins
  `tests/pins.json`'s gradient entries.
- `serde_json` with `preserve_order`: JSON key order is part of the
  contract (the Diagnostic's and TextMetrics' keys; a module's schema).
- `sha2`: the Library's content version.
- `svgtypes` 0.16.1 (usvg 0.48.1's own pin): parse `font-family` exactly as
  usvg does, so the scan agrees with usvg on what failed; and its
  named-colour table (`__namedColour`), so a colour name means what usvg
  draws.
- `simplecss` 0.2 (usvg's own pin; usvg does not re-export it): read
  `<style>` sheets and `style` attributes as usvg does.
- `rquickjs` 0.14.0 with `loader` only: quickjs-ng 0.16.2, vendored and
  built by `rquickjs-sys`. `loader` exists for `set_loader`; the resolver
  and loader installed refuse every specifier, and none of rquickjs's own
  loaders (which reach the file system) is used.
- `png` 0.18 (tiny-skia 0.12's own decoder, already in the lock): decode as
  `Pixmap::decode_png` does and write the stored copy (G-39); still the
  pins' PNG dump.
- `zune-jpeg` 0.5 (resvg 0.48.1's own JPEG decoder): decode as resvg does,
  so a JPEG's copy is checked against resvg's own pixels.
- `imagesize` 0.15 (usvg's own size reader): check a copy's size reads the
  same as its original's.
- Dev: `flate2`, to gzip an `.svgz` asset in a test.

verdicts.closest_existing: The recorder's Show Clicks: ScreenCaptureKit draws the pointer and a click ring into the pixels (RecordingSetup.swift lines 223-224: stream.showsCursor = true, stream.showMouseClicks = choice.showClicks). Also the manual Zoom to Region / add_zoom_action (core/src/edit_zoom.rs), the bundled Keyboard keys template (keys prop) and speed ramps (add_speed_ramp). No cursor, click or key events are stored anywhere: no NSEvent.mouseLocation, global monitor, CGEvent tap or NSCursor read exists in app/Sources.
verdicts.feasibility: Feasible, but it is a road map, not a planner over existing ops. Capture: NSEvent.mouseLocation sampled per frame, a global NSEvent monitor for clicks, a listen-only CGEvent tap for keys (Input Monitoring, CGPreflightListenEventAccess/CGRequestListenEventAccess, macOS 10.15+), NSCursor.currentSystem for the cursor image (macOS 10.6+, but Apple's availability metadata marks it deprecated in macOS 27.0, so it needs a replacement plan). Timing can anchor on the screen's first-frame PTS: the camera-recording spike measured E2 within 0.5 ms of truth on the host clock, which is the clock NSEvent timestamps use, so #370 (a microphone-offset problem) is not inherited. Core: a cursor source or recipe layer plus a format bump, smoothing and spring arithmetic in a new module, an auto-zoom planner emitting add_zoom_action and a typing planner emitting speed actions and Keyboard keys graphic clips. Hard part the candidate understates: the cursor must follow the screen clip's evaluated transform, including its zoom actions. A sprite on another track would not, so it needs either a source drawn as part of the screen clip's layer or a nest around screen plus cursor with the zooms on the nest. Consolidate and Relink must carry the non-regenerable sidecar (MediaConsolidator copies media files only). Architectural conflict: spec §11 recording.md decides that what ScreenCaptureKit draws (the cursor and click ring) is taken and 'nothing is reconstructed afterwards', that 'callouts stay OUT' (named there as a metadata format plus an Input Monitoring grant), and that 'a recording is ordinary media: no source kind, no flag, no schema bump'. RecorderStatusItem.swift deliberately avoids an Input Monitoring grant. C2 reverses all three, so the owner must amend §11 first, as CAM-1 did for the camera.
verdicts.platform_apis: ScreenCaptureKit SCStreamConfiguration.showsCursor and showMouseClicks (already used; turn them off when cursor capture is on); NSEvent.mouseLocation and NSEvent.addGlobalMonitorForEvents (AppKit); CGEvent.tapCreate(.listenOnly) with CGPreflightListenEventAccess / CGRequestListenEventAccess (CoreGraphics, macOS 10.15+, confirmed in Apple docs); NSCursor.currentSystem (AppKit, macOS 10.6+, deprecated in 27.0 per Apple's availability metadata). Existing modules: edit_zoom.rs add_zoom_action, edit_action_ramp.rs add_speed_ramp, the keyboard-keys.js template, MediaConsolidator, edit_relink.rs.
verdicts.market_refutation_attempt: Tried to refute on two grounds, commoditisation and the claimed uniqueness. Commoditisation holds: OpenScreen is free, MIT-licensed and has 40.0k GitHub stars (its repo is now archived, with a successor at getopenscreen/openscreen), and it ships auto zoom that follows the cursor, cursor size and smoothing, and click effects. Cap (AGPLv3 apart from its MIT camera and scap crates, 24.2k stars), Recordly (an AGPL fork of OpenScreen), Capptivo, FocuSee and Camtasia all ship click-driven zoom. So the rationale's 'the free Screen Studio … no rival can claim' line is false on 'free'; only 'a full NLE that agents can drive' is distinctive. Demand survives the attempt: Screen Studio sustains $29/month (or $9/month billed yearly) and has stopped selling its lifetime licence to new buyers (secondhand sources), and the free clones drew tens of thousands of stars. Screen recording is Frame Job's home segment, and its recordings are worse than every polished recorder's without cursor data. So this is table stakes for its own users, not a differentiator. Keystroke overlays: Cap's docs mention a keyboard track. Tella's and FocuSee's keystroke overlays were not verified.
verdicts.corrections: (1) Spec §11 recording.md conflicts in three ways: the cursor and click ring burned in by ScreenCaptureKit are the decided design ('nothing is reconstructed afterwards'), 'callouts stay OUT', and a recording carries 'no source kind, no flag, no schema bump'. An owner amendment is needed before any code. (2) #370 is about the microphone file's offset (did-start callback against startPTS). The screen's first-frame PTS was measured within 0.5 ms, so cursor-event alignment does not inherit it. (3) 'One more sprite layer' understates the work: the cursor must follow the screen clip's transform and zoom actions, so it needs a layer drawn with the screen clip or a nest. (4) NSCursor.currentSystem is deprecated as of macOS 27.0. (5) OpenScreen (MIT, 40.0k stars) already claims 'free Screen Studio'. Cap is AGPLv3 (24.2k stars). (6) The Keyboard keys template's keys prop is animate:false and the template is 90 frames, so each shortcut needs one graphic clip. The claims about add_zoom_action, Consolidate carrying only media files, and the absence of event storage are confirmed.

verdicts.closest_existing: Chroma Key (green screen) on video and image clips; matte tracks with Alpha, Inverted Alpha, Luma and Inverted Luma modes (core/src/recipe_matte.rs, model_matte.rs); Clip ▸ Add Background (solid, image, blurred copy); animatable crop, corner radius, shadow and transform; the Window frame graphic template; per-media speech spans (media_speech.rs, audio_duck_speech.rs speech_in_clip); the derived-media render pattern (ReverseRenderer and ReverseCache, IsolationCache, RampAudioCache, RampAudioRenders, MediaCacheLane, BackgroundRender). No ML mask exists. The recorded camera lands on one front Camera track fixed in the bottom-right corner (CAM-10, a decided limit). Issue #124 (Remove Background through Vision) is open, labelled icebox and low-priority, and sits in the Post Release project.
verdicts.feasibility: Feasible on Apple frameworks with no shipped model. VNGeneratePersonSegmentationRequest is confirmed on macOS 12.0+ in Apple's docs, with fast, balanced and accurate quality levels. VNGenerateForegroundInstanceMaskRequest is confirmed on macOS 14.0+, but #124's spike already dropped it for video (up to 57 % of pixels flip between masks 0.1 s apart), so non-person cutout is stills only. What #124 measured: person masks are always 4:3, 512×384 at balanced and 2016×1512 at accurate; accurate runs at 1.7× realtime and takes 1.7 GiB per minute; .fast is stateful; GPU and ANE results differ by up to 25 levels; backlit, from-behind and small figures are missed. Hair and edge quality at these sizes is the real risk, and an edge-refinement pass (for example a guided filter in Metal) is likely needed. That is still a spike, as the candidate says. Placement: a mask movie on a Luma matte track over the camera clip needs no format change, but it is fragile. A matte cuts the track behind it per instant and no clip names another, and Clip.linked pairs only a picture with its sound. So every trim, split, speed change or ramp of the camera clip must be mirrored on the mask clip or they drift. A per-layer mask texture (format bump) is the sound design. #124's plan to bind the mask at texture(2) is stale: texture(2) now holds the look lattice and texture(3) the curves strip. Each mask clip also counts against the 8-track decoder budget (a plan warning, not a refusal). Layouts are action presets over transform, crop, corner radius and shadow, all animatable today. Hide-while-silent must read the MICROPHONE media's speech: a camera recording has no sound of its own and its microphone is a separate file on a Microphone track. media.speech is written only by Duck by Speech's set_media_speech, though the VAD cache exists per media. verdicts.closest_existing: Five word-caption styles plus Subtitles (CaptionStyle.swift has six cases) and three looks (slide, fill, dim; CaptionLooks.swift); four hard-coded text presets (TextPane.swift TextPreset.all: Title, Subtitle, Lower Third, Caption); Edit ▸ Paste Attributes (⌥⌘V), which copies a clip's whole property groups onto other clips, a session-only 'apply style'; 23 bundled graphic templates with accent colour props (graphics, not project templates); File ▸ Duplicate (⇧⌘S) opens a project copy as untitled; ExportPresetsStore.swift as a pattern for a user store. verdicts.feasibility: Feasible with existing pieces, but it meets two spec decisions. verdicts.closest_existing: CaptionExporter.swift writes a caption track as SRT or WebVTT (export_captions). CaptionImporter.swift reads SubRip only (the guide says a .vtt is not read as WebVTT). Captions are transcribed on-device in any language the Mac's recogniser supports, or by AssemblyAI in 21 languages plus auto-detect. Nothing imports the Translation framework. No export writes a soft subtitle track: no tx3g, AVMediaType.text or .subtitle writer, and no subtitle track in core/src/webm_writer.rs.
verdicts.feasibility: Feasible. TranslationSession.init(installedSource:target:) is confirmed in Apple's docs as macOS 26.0+, with an overload taking preferredStrategy, whose highFidelity option uses Apple Intelligence where available. Apple's discussion says it works only for languages already installed. To get the person's permission to download a language, the app must use a session from SwiftUI's translationTask, so this AppKit app needs an NSHostingView-hosted translationTask in the sheet for downloads. Coverage is Apple Translate's language set (about 20, from memory), far short of Submagic's 123. Translating whole sentences and re-paging fits CaptionPages. Word styles get no real word times for a translation: a character-share estimate makes karaoke highlighting arbitrary across languages with different word order, so translated word captions are weak and Subtitles is the honest fallback. Soft tracks: AVAssetWriter can write a text or subtitle (tx3g) track in MOV and MP4, and WebM needs a new S_TEXT/WEBVTT track in core/src/webm_writer.rs. That is new export plumbing in a file family already heavy with rules. WebVTT import is a small CaptionImporter addition.
verdicts.platform_apis: Translation framework TranslationSession init(installedSource:target:) and init(installedSource:target:preferredStrategy:) (macOS 26.0+, confirmed in Apple docs; downloads only through SwiftUI translationTask); AVAssetWriterInput with a text or subtitle media type (tx3g) for MOV and MP4; core webm_writer.rs for a WebVTT track; existing CaptionExporter (SRT, VTT), CaptionImporter (SRT), CaptionPages.
verdicts.market_refutation_attempt: Refuted on the main supporting claims. (a) The 'more than 25% of watch time from non-primary languages' figure, from YouTube's pilot (15%+ in 2023), is about multi-language AUDIO tracks, meaning dubs, not subtitles. (b) The platforms commoditise translation themselves: YouTube auto-dubbing reached every Partner Program channel in 2025 and now covers 27 languages, and viewers can auto-translate captions in the player. So a creator gets translation free at the destination, and burned-in translated captions for social are one language per upload. (c) ADA Title II's WCAG 2.1 AA requires captions in the spoken language, which Frame Job already makes; translation does not serve that requirement. (d) Descript's 'more languages' request is about transcription coverage, not translation. (e) Embedded soft subtitle tracks matter mainly to downloaded files and desktop players; YouTube, Vimeo and LMSs ingest sidecar SRT or VTT, which Frame Job already writes. What survives: Premiere ships caption translation into 27 languages (cloud, Google and Microsoft), so pro NLEs see it as table stakes, and a free on-device version is a nice line. It is a cheap add-on, not something that pushes Frame Job toward leading for creators. The market case does not survive.
verdicts.corrections: (1) The 25% YouTube statistic concerns dubbed audio tracks, not subtitles. (2) The headless TranslationSession cannot download languages; that needs SwiftUI's translationTask, hostable in AppKit through NSHostingView. (3) Apple's language set is about 20, not comparable with Submagic's 123 (from memory, not re-verified). (4) ADA Title II requires same-language captions, which Frame Job already makes. The compliance dates are, from memory, April 2026 for large public entities and April 2027 for small ones; this could not be re-verified because the session's web-search budget ran out. So '26 April 2027' applies only to smaller entities. (5) 'Final Cut Pro announced 23 more caption languages' was not verified and most likely refers to transcription languages, not translation. (6) Descript's ~400-vote request is for more transcription languages. Confirmed: SRT and VTT export, SRT-only import (a .vtt 'is not read as WebVTT'), no Translation import, no soft subtitle tracks in MOV, MP4 or WebM. If ever built, this is a phase inside a caption or export road map, not a bet of its own.

verdicts.closest_existing: The recorder (screen, camera and microphone through one panel); get_transcript (a clip's words in a from/to window, cached per media, on-device); the assistant's false-start cuts through get_transcript and ripple_delete_ranges; Remove Filler Words and Remove Silences. There is no teleprompter, no script field in the project model, and no live recognition.
verdicts.feasibility: Feasible but larger than it looks. SpeechEngine.swift today runs SpeechAnalyzer.analyzeSequence over an extracted 16 kHz WAV file with reportingOptions [], so it is file-based only and has no live or volatile path. The claim that it 'can run live during a recording' is false for the code. The framework does support live input: a stream of AnalyzerInput buffers from an AVAudioEngine tap, converted to the analyzer's format, with .volatileResults (per third-party guides; about 0.3-0.5 s to the first volatile result reported on iPhone). A live path would also contend with the recorder's own microphone capture session and must keep async confined to SpeechEngine.swift (spec §11 W-8). Hiding the teleprompter from the recording is already free: the recorder excludes Frame Job's windows unless 'Include Frame Job windows' is ticked. The script becomes a project field (format bump). Script-to-word alignment is pure Rust sequence alignment, and assembly is ordinary ops (ripple_delete_ranges, move_clip). Choosing the 'best take' (fewest fillers, no stumble) overlaps C1's retake detection, and fillers come only from the cloud AssemblyAI transcript (TR-*: filler removal is cloud-only), so on-device takes would be judged with less signal.
verdicts.platform_apis: Speech framework SpeechAnalyzer and SpeechTranscriber with AnalyzerInput streaming and reportingOptions .volatileResults (macOS 26; live use verified only through third-party guides, since the search budget ran out before Apple's docs were fetched); AVAudioEngine input tap with AVAudioConverter; the existing recorder panel's window exclusion; core: a new alignment module, ripple_delete_ranges.
verdicts.market_refutation_attempt: Refuted. (a) The teleprompter half is commoditised: Descript has a built-in teleprompter hidden from desktop capture, Tella has speaker notes, and free or cheap Mac apps (the open-source NotchPrompter with voice activation, NotchPrompt with live word tracking, Notchie that scrolls with speech) sit beside any recorder. (b) The assembly half: Resolve IntelliScript matches takes to a script and builds a rough cut, but it is Studio-only ($295) and its forum has reports of it failing to build timelines. 'Premiere Paper Edit' is not a native feature; a 2026 Adobe community thread asks for it and points to third-party Sheetscut. Script-first recording suits a minority of creators (scripted explainers, courses), while most talking-head and screencast creators improvise. The NUS 2025 'time is the barrier' study could not be verified, and even if true it argues for faster cleanup generally, which C1's retake removal serves without asking creators to write a script. Prequel's and Cap's teleprompters were not confirmed, and Loom reportedly has none, so 'they have teleprompters but no assembly' is partly unfounded. The distinctive end-to-end loop is real but niche.
verdicts.corrections: (1) SpeechEngine.swift is file-based (analyzeSequence over an extracted WAV, reportingOptions []) and has no live recognition today; the framework supports it, but it is new work under W-8's async confinement. (2) 'Premiere Paper Edit' does not exist as a native Premiere feature. (3) Resolve IntelliScript is Studio-only, with reliability complaints. (4) Prequel's voice-tracking notch teleprompter and Cap's teleprompter were not confirmed; Descript and Tella do have teleprompters, and free notch teleprompters with voice tracking exist. (5) Filler detection is cloud-only (AssemblyAI disfluencies), so 'fewest fillers' cannot be judged on-device. (6) Hiding the teleprompter from capture already works through the recorder's exclusion of Frame Job windows. Its valuable kernel, best-take and retake removal, belongs to C1.

verdicts.closest_existing: The recorder's Show Clicks: ScreenCaptureKit draws the pointer and a click ring into the pixels (RecordingSetup.swift lines 223-224: stream.showsCursor = true, stream.showMouseClicks = choice.showClicks). Also the manual Zoom to Region / add_zoom_action (core/src/edit_zoom.rs), the bundled Keyboard keys template (keys prop) and speed ramps (add_speed_ramp). No cursor, click or key events are stored anywhere: no NSEvent.mouseLocation, global monitor, CGEvent tap or NSCursor read exists in app/Sources.
verdicts.feasibility: Feasible, but it is a road map, not a planner over existing ops. Capture: NSEvent.mouseLocation sampled per frame, a global NSEvent monitor for clicks, a listen-only CGEvent tap for keys (Input Monitoring, CGPreflightListenEventAccess/CGRequestListenEventAccess, macOS 10.15+), NSCursor.currentSystem for the cursor image (macOS 10.6+, but Apple's availability metadata marks it deprecated in macOS 27.0, so it needs a replacement plan). Timing can anchor on the screen's first-frame PTS: the camera-recording spike measured E2 within 0.5 ms of truth on the host clock, which is the clock NSEvent timestamps use, so #370 (a microphone-offset problem) is not inherited. Core: a cursor source or recipe layer plus a format bump, smoothing and spring arithmetic in a new module, an auto-zoom planner emitting add_zoom_action and a typing planner emitting speed actions and Keyboard keys graphic clips. Hard part the candidate understates: the cursor must follow the screen clip's evaluated transform, including its zoom actions. A sprite on another track would not, so it needs either a source drawn as part of the screen clip's layer or a nest around screen plus cursor with the zooms on the nest. Consolidate and Relink must carry the non-regenerable sidecar (MediaConsolidator copies media files only). Architectural conflict: spec §11 recording.md decides that what ScreenCaptureKit draws (the cursor and click ring) is taken and 'nothing is reconstructed afterwards', that 'callouts stay OUT' (named there as a metadata format plus an Input Monitoring grant), and that 'a recording is ordinary media: no source kind, no flag, no schema bump'. RecorderStatusItem.swift deliberately avoids an Input Monitoring grant. C2 reverses all three, so the owner must amend §11 first, as CAM-1 did for the camera.
verdicts.platform_apis: ScreenCaptureKit SCStreamConfiguration.showsCursor and showMouseClicks (already used; turn them off when cursor capture is on); NSEvent.mouseLocation and NSEvent.addGlobalMonitorForEvents (AppKit); CGEvent.tapCreate(.listenOnly) with CGPreflightListenEventAccess / CGRequestListenEventAccess (CoreGraphics, macOS 10.15+, confirmed in Apple docs); NSCursor.currentSystem (AppKit, macOS 10.6+, deprecated in 27.0 per Apple's availability metadata). Existing modules: edit_zoom.rs add_zoom_action, edit_action_ramp.rs add_speed_ramp, the keyboard-keys.js template, MediaConsolidator, edit_relink.rs.
verdicts.market_refutation_attempt: Tried to refute on two grounds, commoditisation and the claimed uniqueness. Commoditisation holds: OpenScreen is free, MIT-licensed and has 40.0k GitHub stars (its repo is now archived, with a successor at getopenscreen/openscreen), and it ships auto zoom that follows the cursor, cursor size and smoothing, and click effects. Cap (AGPLv3 apart from its MIT camera and scap crates, 24.2k stars), Recordly (an AGPL fork of OpenScreen), Capptivo, FocuSee and Camtasia all ship click-driven zoom. So the rationale's 'the free Screen Studio … no rival can claim' line is false on 'free'; only 'a full NLE that agents can drive' is distinctive. Demand survives the attempt: Screen Studio sustains $29/month (or $9/month billed yearly) and has stopped selling its lifetime licence to new buyers (secondhand sources), and the free clones drew tens of thousands of stars. Screen recording is Frame Job's home segment, and its recordings are worse than every polished recorder's without cursor data. So this is table stakes for its own users, not a differentiator. Keystroke overlays: Cap's docs mention a keyboard track. Tella's and FocuSee's keystroke overlays were not verified.
verdicts.corrections: (1) Spec §11 recording.md conflicts in three ways: the cursor and click ring burned in by ScreenCaptureKit are the decided design ('nothing is reconstructed afterwards'), 'callouts stay OUT', and a recording carries 'no source kind, no flag, no schema bump'. An owner amendment is needed before any code. (2) #370 is about the microphone file's offset (did-start callback against startPTS). The screen's first-frame PTS was measured within 0.5 ms, so cursor-event alignment does not inherit it. (3) 'One more sprite layer' understates the work: the cursor must follow the screen clip's transform and zoom actions, so it needs a layer drawn with the screen clip or a nest. (4) NSCursor.currentSystem is deprecated as of macOS 27.0. (5) OpenScreen (MIT, 40.0k stars) already claims 'free Screen Studio'. Cap is AGPLv3 (24.2k stars). (6) The Keyboard keys template's keys prop is animate:false and the template is 90 frames, so each shortcut needs one graphic clip. The claims about add_zoom_action, Consolidate carrying only media files, and the absence of event storage are confirmed.

verdicts.closest_existing: CaptionExporter.swift writes a caption track as SRT or WebVTT (export_captions). CaptionImporter.swift reads SubRip only (the guide says a .vtt is not read as WebVTT). Captions are transcribed on-device in any language the Mac's recogniser supports, or by AssemblyAI in 21 languages plus auto-detect. Nothing imports the Translation framework. verdicts.feasibility: Feasible. TranslationSession.init(installedSource:target:) is confirmed in Apple's docs as macOS 26.0+, with an overload taking preferredStrategy, whose highFidelity option uses Apple Intelligence where available. Apple's discussion says it works only for languages already installed. To get the person's permission to download a language, the app must use a session from SwiftUI's translationTask, so this AppKit app needs an NSHostingView-hosted translationTask in the sheet for downloads. Coverage is Apple Translate's language set (about 20, from memory), far short of Submagic's 123. Translating whole sentences and re-paging fits CaptionPages. Word styles get no real word times for a translation: a character-share estimate makes karaoke highlighting arbitrary across languages with different word order, so translated word captions are weak and Subtitles is the honest fallback. verdicts.market_refutation_attempt: Refuted on the main supporting claims. (a) The 'more than 25% of watch time from non-primary languages' figure, from YouTube's pilot (15%+ in 2023), is about multi-language AUDIO tracks, meaning dubs, not subtitles. So a creator gets translation free at the destination, and burned-in translated captions for social are one language per upload. (c) ADA Title II's WCAG 2.1 AA requires captions in the spoken language, which Frame Job already makes; translation does not serve that requirement. The compliance dates are, from memory, April 2026 for large public entities and April 2027 for small ones; this could not be re-verified because the session's web-search budget ran out. So '26 April 2027' applies only to smaller entities. (5) 'Final Cut Pro announced 23 more caption languages' was not verified and most likely refers to transcription languages, not translation. verdicts.closest_existing: The recorder (screen, camera and microphone through one panel); get_transcript (a clip's words in a from/to window, cached per media, on-device); the assistant's false-start cuts through get_transcript and ripple_delete_ranges; Remove Filler Words and Remove Silences. There is no teleprompter, no script field in the project model, and no live recognition.
verdicts.feasibility: Feasible but larger than it looks. SpeechEngine.swift today runs SpeechAnalyzer.analyzeSequence over an extracted 16 kHz WAV file with reportingOptions [], so it is file-based only and has no live or volatile path. The claim that it 'can run live during a recording' is false for the code. The framework does support live input: a stream of AnalyzerInput buffers from an AVAudioEngine tap, converted to the analyzer's format, with .volatileResults (per third-party guides; about 0.3-0.5 s to the first volatile result reported on iPhone). A live path would also contend with the recorder's own microphone capture session and must keep async confined to SpeechEngine.swift (spec §11 W-8). Hiding the teleprompter from the recording is already free: the recorder excludes Frame Job's windows unless 'Include Frame Job windows' is ticked. The script becomes a project field (format bump). Script-to-word alignment is pure Rust sequence alignment, and assembly is ordinary ops (ripple_delete_ranges, move_clip). Choosing the 'best take' (fewest fillers, no stumble) overlaps C1's retake detection, and fillers come only from the cloud AssemblyAI transcript (TR-*: filler removal is cloud-only), so on-device takes would be judged with less signal.
verdicts.platform_apis: Speech framework SpeechAnalyzer and SpeechTranscriber with AnalyzerInput streaming and reportingOptions .volatileResults (macOS 26; live use verified only through third-party guides, since the search budget ran out before Apple's docs were fetched); AVAudioEngine input tap with AVAudioConverter; the existing recorder panel's window exclusion; core: a new alignment module, ripple_delete_ranges.

Script-first recording suits a minority of creators (scripted explainers, courses), while most talking-head and screencast creators improvise. verdicts.closest_existing: The recorder's Show Clicks: ScreenCaptureKit draws the pointer and a click ring into the pixels (RecordingSetup.swift lines 223-224: stream.showsCursor = true, stream.showMouseClicks = choice.showClicks). Also the manual Zoom to Region / add_zoom_action (core/src/edit_zoom.rs), the bundled Keyboard keys template (keys prop) and speed ramps (add_speed_ramp). No cursor, click or key events are stored anywhere: no NSEvent.mouseLocation, global monitor, CGEvent tap or NSCursor read exists in app/Sources.
verdicts.feasibility: Feasible, but it is a road map, not a planner over existing ops. Capture: NSEvent.mouseLocation sampled per frame, a global NSEvent monitor for clicks, a listen-only CGEvent tap for keys (Input Monitoring, CGPreflightListenEventAccess/CGRequestListenEventAccess, macOS 10.15+), NSCursor.currentSystem for the cursor image (macOS 10.6+, but Apple's availability metadata marks it deprecated in macOS 27.0, so it needs a replacement plan). Timing can anchor on the screen's first-frame PTS: the camera-recording spike measured E2 within 0.5 ms of truth on the host clock, which is the clock NSEvent timestamps use, so #370 (a microphone-offset problem) is not inherited. Core: a cursor source or recipe layer plus a format bump, smoothing and spring arithmetic in a new module, an auto-zoom planner emitting add_zoom_action and a typing planner emitting speed actions and Keyboard keys graphic clips. Hard part the candidate understates: the cursor must follow the screen clip's evaluated transform, including its zoom actions. A sprite on another track would not, so it needs either a source drawn as part of the screen clip's layer or a nest around screen plus cursor with the zooms on the nest. Consolidate and Relink must carry the non-regenerable sidecar (MediaConsolidator copies media files only). Architectural conflict: spec §11 recording.md decides that what ScreenCaptureKit draws (the cursor and click ring) is taken and 'nothing is reconstructed afterwards', that 'callouts stay OUT' (named there as a metadata format plus an Input Monitoring grant), and that 'a recording is ordinary media: no source kind, no flag, no schema bump'. RecorderStatusItem.swift deliberately avoids an Input Monitoring grant. C2 reverses all three, so the owner must amend §11 first, as CAM-1 did for the camera.

verdicts.market_refutation_attempt: Tried to refute on two grounds, commoditisation and the claimed uniqueness. Commoditisation holds: OpenScreen is free, MIT-licensed and has 40.0k GitHub stars (its repo is now archived, with a successor at getopenscreen/openscreen), and it ships auto zoom that follows the cursor, cursor size and smoothing, and click effects. Cap (AGPLv3 apart from its MIT camera and scap crates, 24.2k stars), Recordly (an AGPL fork of OpenScreen), Capptivo, FocuSee and Camtasia all ship click-driven zoom. So the rationale's 'the free Screen Studio … no rival can claim' line is false on 'free'; only 'a full NLE that agents can drive' is distinctive. Demand survives the attempt: Screen Studio sustains $29/month (or $9/month billed yearly) and has stopped selling its lifetime licence to new buyers (secondhand sources), and the free clones drew tens of thousands of stars. Screen recording is Frame Job's home segment, and its recordings are worse than every polished recorder's without cursor data. So this is table stakes for its own users, not a differentiator. Keystroke overlays: Cap's docs mention a keyboard track. Tella's and FocuSee's keystroke overlays were not verified.
verdicts.corrections: (1) Spec §11 recording.md conflicts in three ways: the cursor and click ring burned in by ScreenCaptureKit are the decided design ('nothing is reconstructed afterwards'), 'callouts stay OUT', and a recording carries 'no source kind, no flag, no schema bump'. An owner amendment is needed before any code. (2) #370 is about the microphone file's offset (did-start callback against startPTS). The screen's first-frame PTS was measured within 0.5 ms, so cursor-event alignment does not inherit it. (3) 'One more sprite layer' understates the work: the cursor must follow the screen clip's transform and zoom actions, so it needs a layer drawn with the screen clip or a nest. (4) NSCursor.currentSystem is deprecated as of macOS 27.0. (5) OpenScreen (MIT, 40.0k stars) already claims 'free Screen Studio'. Cap is AGPLv3 (24.2k stars). (6) The Keyboard keys template's keys prop is animate:false and the template is 90 frames, so each shortcut needs one graphic clip. The claims about add_zoom_action, Consolidate carrying only media files, and the absence of event storage are confirmed.

verdicts.closest_existing: Chroma Key (green screen) on video and image clips; matte tracks with Alpha, Inverted Alpha, Luma and Inverted Luma modes (core/src/recipe_matte.rs, model_matte.rs); Clip ▸ Add Background (solid, image, blurred copy); animatable crop, corner radius, shadow and transform; the Window frame graphic template; per-media speech spans (media_speech.rs, audio_duck_speech.rs speech_in_clip); the derived-media render pattern (ReverseRenderer and ReverseCache, IsolationCache, RampAudioCache, RampAudioRenders, MediaCacheLane, BackgroundRender). verdicts.feasibility: Feasible on Apple frameworks with no shipped model. VNGeneratePersonSegmentationRequest is confirmed on macOS 12.0+ in Apple's docs, with fast, balanced and accurate quality levels. VNGenerateForegroundInstanceMaskRequest is confirmed on macOS 14.0+, but #124's spike already dropped it for video (up to 57 % of pixels flip between masks 0.1 s apart), so non-person cutout is stills only. What #124 measured: person masks are always 4:3, 512×384 at balanced and 2016×1512 at accurate; accurate runs at 1.7× realtime and takes 1.7 GiB per minute; .fast is stateful; GPU and ANE results differ by up to 25 levels; backlit, from-behind and small figures are missed. Hair and edge quality at these sizes is the real risk, and an edge-refinement pass (for example a guided filter in Metal) is likely needed. That is still a spike, as the candidate says. Placement: a mask movie on a Luma matte track over the camera clip needs no format change, but it is fragile. A matte cuts the track behind it per instant and no clip names another, and Clip.linked pairs only a picture with its sound. So every trim, split, speed change or ramp of the camera clip must be mirrored on the mask clip or they drift. A per-layer mask texture (format bump) is the sound design. #124's plan to bind the mask at texture(2) is stale: texture(2) now holds the look lattice and texture(3) the curves strip. Each mask clip also counts against the 8-track decoder budget (a plan warning, not a refusal). Layouts are action presets over transform, crop, corner radius and shadow, all animatable today. Hide-while-silent must read the MICROPHONE media's speech: a camera recording has no sound of its own and its microphone is a separate file on a Microphone track. media.speech is written only by Duck by Speech's set_media_speech, though the VAD cache exists per media. Spec §1 lists ML and heavy pixel work as non-goals, and #124's proposed decision D5 must enter §11 first. The owner has said these limits may be lifted.
verdicts.platform_apis: Vision VNGeneratePersonSegmentationRequest (macOS 12.0+, confirmed in Apple docs; qualityLevel .fast, .balanced, .accurate); VNGenerateForegroundInstanceMaskRequest (macOS 14.0+, confirmed, but flickers on video per #124's spike); AVAssetWriter for an 8-bit grey or alpha HEVC mask; existing modules: ReverseRenderer and ReverseCache, RampAudioRenders, MediaCacheLedger, BackgroundRender, recipe_matte.rs (Luma matte), audio_duck_speech.rs speech_in_clip, actions (transform, crop, corner radius, shadow).
verdicts.market_refutation_attempt: Tried to refute this as niche or distrusted. Evidence says it is table stakes in 2026 rather than niche. Screen Studio 4.0 (5 Oct 2026, per AlternativeTo) shipped camera cutout as a local beta, split-screen layouts that put the presenter beside or above the recording, 'Hide during silence', and face tracking. Tella sells background removal. Premiere's Object Mask came out of beta in Premiere 26 (Jan 2026) and runs on-device; Final Cut Pro has had Magnetic Mask since FCP 11; Resolve has Magic Mask. Distrust exists (beta labels, edge-quality complaints, Premiere beta reports of variable-frame-rate tracking problems), but that argues for doing it well, not against demand. Commoditised, so it does not differentiate. Still, Frame Job already records a camera beside the screen and pins it to one corner, which makes it visibly behind every 2026 recorder. Holds up as catch-up for its home segment.
verdicts.corrections: (1) Effort is a road map (L), not M: cutout (spike, render cache, a mask that follows edits, HLG working space) is M on its own, and layouts plus hide-while-silent are another phase or two. (2) Non-person cutout through VNGenerateForegroundInstanceMaskRequest was already ruled out for video by #124's spike because of flicker. (3) #124's texture(2) binding is stale: looks hold texture(2) and curves texture(3). (4) The camera clip has no audio, so hide-while-silent reads the microphone media's spans mapped through the microphone clip, not speech_in_clip on the camera clip. (5) A mask on a Luma matte track has no link to the camera clip and desyncs on trims, splits and speed changes; 'no format change' holds only for a fragile first phase. (6) Partial pieces already exist: chroma key, mattes, Add Background, corner radius and shadow, the Window frame template. (7) Confirmed: #124 is open and iceboxed, the camera is fixed bottom-right (CAM-10), the 8-track decoder budget is a warning, and transform, crop, corner radius and shadow animate. 'Comparable to Screen Studio's hair quality' is unverified; the spike's 512×384 balanced masks suggest it is not without refinement.

verdicts.closest_existing: Five word-caption styles plus Subtitles (CaptionStyle.swift has six cases) and three looks (slide, fill, dim; CaptionLooks.swift); four hard-coded text presets (TextPane.swift TextPreset.all: Title, Subtitle, Lower Third, Caption); Edit ▸ Paste Attributes (⌥⌘V), which copies a clip's whole property groups onto other clips, a session-only 'apply style'; 23 bundled graphic templates with accent colour props (graphics, not project templates); File ▸ Duplicate (⇧⌘S) opens a project copy as untitled; ExportPresetsStore.swift as a pattern for a user store. There is no saved style, brand kit, New from Template, keyword emphasis or emoji, and no inspector control for a page's word style.
verdicts.feasibility: Feasible with existing pieces, but it meets two spec decisions. (a) Spec §11 W-10 says set_text may patch word_style as the agent's door, 'not a promise that a hand-restyled page still fits: restyling is regenerating', and app/CLAUDE.md says nothing in the inspector writes word_style (CaptionLayout.place is its one app-side writer). Pages are measured at the style's size and font, so inspector size or font controls on placed pages would have to re-page through the Replace path or amend W-10. Colours alone do not move a glyph and are safe. (b) Per-word emphasis needs a parallel per-token list in model_words.rs and a format bump, kept to W-2's token count (split_whitespace) and W-3's rebasing. Saved styles: a user store modelled on ExportPresetsStore. Templates: a consolidated .framejob opened as untitled through the Duplicate path, with new_project gaining a template argument. Keyword picking: NaturalLanguage NLTagger (on-device) or the Assistant. Emoji: CoreText falls back to Apple Color Emoji in the text path, but whether colour emoji survive the HLG lift and the backdrop or outline paths is unverified. MCP mirrors (list_styles and apply_style) are straightforward.
verdicts.platform_apis: NaturalLanguage NLTagger (name and number tagging, on-device); CoreText with Apple Color Emoji fallback in LayerRenderersText; existing modules: CaptionLayout.place (the one word_style writer), CaptionPages (the pager), model_words.rs WordStyle, actions_color.rs, ExportPresetsStore.swift, File ▸ Duplicate, MediaConsolidator, paste_attributes.
verdicts.market_refutation_attempt: Tried to refute it as commoditised and as not Frame Job's gap. It is commoditised: CapCut (free), Submagic (up to three highlight colours, manual and auto emoji), Descript (presets, plus 18 new designs per a news site), Captions.ai, OpusClip and Choppity (a brand template manager, Aug 2026) all ship caption presets, emphasis and brand templates. The cited Premiere request (about 380 upvotes in an Oct 2026 community post; the 416 figure was not confirmed) asks for animated word captions, which Frame Job already ships, so it does not support C8's increment. What survives: repeat creators re-do caption looks, emphasis and intros on every episode. Descript's 'default settings for fancy captions' request and the brand-template managers show saving a style is wanted. Frame Job today cannot restyle a placed word page at all in the inspector (guide: 'There is no inspector section for a page's word style'). Holds up as table-stakes catch-up for short-form and repeat creators, not as a reason anyone switches.
verdicts.corrections: (1) word_style is per page (one text clip), not per word: no per-word colour exists anywhere, and an agent can set a page's highlight colour, pop scale and pill colour through set_text's word_style. (4) Paste Attributes already copies a style between clips within a session, and 23 graphic templates exist, so already_have is partial, not none. (5) The Premiere vote count found was about 380 (Oct 2026), and that request is for something Frame Job has. (6) Emoji under HLG is unverified. Confirmed: TextPreset.all holds four hard-coded presets; there is no keyword emphasis or emoji (guide: 'There is no keyword emphasis and no emoji'); per-word emphasis needs a model_words.rs field and a format bump under W-2 and W-3; Duplicate exists and New from Template does not.

Script-first recording suits a minority of creators (scripted explainers, courses), while most talking-head and screencast creators improvise. The NUS 2025 'time is the barrier' study could not be verified, and even if true it argues for faster cleanup generally, which C1's retake removal serves without asking creators to write a script. Prequel's and Cap's teleprompters were not confirmed, and Loom reportedly has none, so 'they have teleprompters but no assembly' is partly unfounded. The distinctive end-to-end loop is real but niche.
verdicts.corrections: (1) SpeechEngine.swift is file-based (analyzeSequence over an extracted WAV, reportingOptions []) and has no live recognition today; the framework supports it, but it is new work under W-8's async confinement. (2) 'Premiere Paper Edit' does not exist as a native Premiere feature. (3) Resolve IntelliScript is Studio-only, with reliability complaints. (4) Prequel's voice-tracking notch teleprompter and Cap's teleprompter were not confirmed; Descript and Tella do have teleprompters, and free notch teleprompters with voice tracking exist. (5) Filler detection is cloud-only (AssemblyAI disfluencies), so 'fewest fillers' cannot be judged on-device. (6) Hiding the teleprompter from capture already works through the recorder's exclusion of Frame Job windows. Its valuable kernel, best-take and retake removal, belongs to C1.
